description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description:

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

704625ad94a7c8bc93f9bea7a0b865b9a0c3d44e
Implement NanoChat Init, muP, complete(d)P (#955)
We implement a few modern parameterization schemes.

For muP and complete(d)P, there is a LR multiplier that gets computed as
models grow. In reference implementations of these schemes, the
multiplier usually grows at the same rate for all matrices (often
tracking the growth of d_model). In our case, different matrices will
sometimes grow at different rates between model sizes, so we provide
functionality to have distinct LR multipliers for each matrix.

[muP paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2203.03466) | [complete(d)P
paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22382)

---------

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

 CHANGELOG.md                                       |    7 +
 src/examples/completedp/__init__.py                |    0
---
diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index a1826d230..23c423313 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -25,9 +25,16 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 - Added an opt-in FP32-output LM head with low-precision GEMMs and mixed-precision backward.
 - Added optional eager-rounding parity and dynamic-row specialization for no-gradient SwiGLU.
 - Added `RoutedExpertsConfig.fused_no_grad_activation` (default `True`). Setting it to `False` makes no-gradient routed-expert forwards use the same eager SiLU-then-multiply activation as the gradient-enabled training path instead of the fused valid-prefix kernel, so policy scoring can share the training forward's arithmetic exactly. Explicit FP8 and wave-kernel callers are unchanged.
+- Added `InitMethod.nanochat`, the nanochat initialization based on the spectral condition for feature learning: each weight matrix uses `std = 1/√fan_in · min(1, √(fan_out/fan_in))`, embeddings use `std = 1.0`, and depthwise convolutions use `std = 1/√kernel_size`. It covers attention, KDA, Gated DeltaNet, dense feed-forward, MoE, and OLMoDDP MoE-v2 blocks. The normalized transformer rejects it, since it normalizes every matrix after initialization.
+- Added muP learning rates for Adam-type optimizers via `MuPConfig`, set as `mup` on any `OptimConfig` (except Muon/Dion) or on `OLMoDDPOptimizerConfig`. Each weight matrix gets `lr * base_width / fan_in`, embeddings get `lr * embedding_lr_multiplier`, and element-wise parameters get `lr`; parameter groups (including `group_overrides`) are split by multiplier when the optimizer is built. Use it with `InitMethod.nanochat`. `named_param_shapes` in `olmo_core.nn.transformer.mup` classifies parameters, and `src/examples/mup/coord_check.py` runs a width coordinate check.
+- Added a base-model mode to `MuPConfig`: `MuPConfig.from_base_model(model)` stores each weight-matrix role's fan-in in a base model as `base_fan_ins`, and each matrix then gets `lr * base_fan_in / fan_in`, so every learning rate is exactly `lr` in the base model. Roles (`named_matrix_roles` in `olmo_core.nn.transformer.mup`) match matrices across models of different width and depth by block kind and path within the block.
+- Added the CompletedP (Complete^(d)P) parameterization from "Completed Hyperparameter Transfer across Modules, Width, Depth, Batch & Duration" (arXiv:2512.22382). Set `TransformerConfig.completedp` (`CompletedPConfig`: `base_width`, `base_depth`, `alpha`) on the model to scale every residual branch by `(n_layers / base_depth) ** -alpha` and the `normal` init of hidden matrices, the LM head and in-block matrices with a fixed output size (MoE routers, KDA `f_proj_1` / `g_proj_1`) by width. Then set `completedp` (`CompletedPOptimConfig`) on `AdamWConfig`, `SkipStepAdamWConfig` or `OLMoDDPOptimizerConfig` to give each parameter group its own learning rate, AdamW epsilon and weight decay by role, width and depth, plus batch-size and training-duration scaling of those and of the betas. Supported for dense default / reordered-norm / peri-norm blocks and OLMoDDP MoE-v2 blocks. `OLMoDDPTransformerBlock` now accepts `attention_residual_alpha` and `feed_forward_residual_alpha`, and folds them into the branch output norm's gains when it can (`LayerNorm.output_scale`, supported by `LayerNorm` and `RMSNorm`). `src/examples/completedp/` has a width/depth coordinate check and a hero-architecture check.
+- Added `CompletedPConfig.from_base_model()`, which records the fan-in of every weight matrix of the base model (`CompletedPConfig.base_block_fan_ins`). Each matrix's width ratio is then its fan-in over the same matrix's fan-in in the base model, instead of over `base_width`, so the base model gets exactly the base init and hyperparameters, including matrices whose fan-in isn't `d_model` (e.g. an MLP's down projection). Configs without `base_block_fan_ins` keep the previous rule and log a warning.
+- Added `CompletedPConfig.fixed_kv_width` (default off). When set, softmax attention's `w_k` and `w_v` are readout matrices, with the output-weight init and epsilon, for models whose key/value width (`n_kv_heads * head_dim`) is the same at every size.
 
 ### Fixed
 
+- The extra token rows of `SplitVocabEmbedding` (`TransformerConfig.n_extra_vocab > 0`) are now initialized by the model's init method like the base rows, instead of always with `init_std`, so they start at the same scale under `nanochat`, `llama`, `llama_depth`, `fan_in` and `normalized` init. The `normal` init is unchanged. muP and CompletedP now classify both rows as embeddings instead of raising.
 - Fixed int32 pointer-offset overflow in the valid-prefix SwiGLU Triton kernels (forward, dynamic-row forward, and backward). Row and column indices are widened to int64 before stride multiplication, so no-gradient MoE activation buffers with 2^31 or more elements (for example 1,048,576 rows by 2,048 BF16 columns) no longer read or write wrapped addresses.
 - Activation checkpointing now preserves the RNG state across recomputation whenever dropout is active (including `ResidualStream.masked_dropout`), so the recomputed forward replays the same dropout masks as the original forward instead of drawing new ones. Previously this was done only for EMO routing.
 - Preserve OLMoDDP inference rounding in newly exported HF models, including packed dense/shared projections, packed SwiGLU, and architecture-specific BF16 TransformerEngine index-map combination; serialize the mode and retain legacy HF configs' existing numerics. CUDA inference without Triton uses the Torch activation fallback.

Implement NanoChat Init, muP, complete(d)P (#955)
We implement a few modern parameterization schemes.

For muP and complete(d)P, there is a LR multiplier that gets computed as
models grow. In reference implementations of these schemes, the
multiplier usually grows at the same rate for all matrices (often
tracking the growth of d_model). In our case, different matrices will
sometimes grow at different rates between model sizes, so we provide
functionality to have distinct LR multipliers for each matrix.

[muP paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2203.03466) | [complete(d)P
paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22382)

---------

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

 CHANGELOG.md                                       |    7 +
 src/examples/completedp/__init__.py                |    0
---
diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index a1826d230..23c423313 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -25,9 +25,16 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 - Added an opt-in FP32-output LM head with low-precision GEMMs and mixed-precision backward.
 - Added optional eager-rounding parity and dynamic-row specialization for no-gradient SwiGLU.
 - Added `RoutedExpertsConfig.fused_no_grad_activation` (default `True`). Setting it to `False` makes no-gradient routed-expert forwards use the same eager SiLU-then-multiply activation as the gradient-enabled training path instead of the fused valid-prefix kernel, so policy scoring can share the training forward's arithmetic exactly. Explicit FP8 and wave-kernel callers are unchanged.
+- Added `InitMethod.nanochat`, the nanochat initialization based on the spectral condition for feature learning: each weight matrix uses `std = 1/√fan_in · min(1, √(fan_out/fan_in))`, embeddings use `std = 1.0`, and depthwise convolutions use `std = 1/√kernel_size`. It covers attention, KDA, Gated DeltaNet, dense feed-forward, MoE, and OLMoDDP MoE-v2 blocks. The normalized transformer rejects it, since it normalizes every matrix after initialization.
+- Added muP learning rates for Adam-type optimizers via `MuPConfig`, set as `mup` on any `OptimConfig` (except Muon/Dion) or on `OLMoDDPOptimizerConfig`. Each weight matrix gets `lr * base_width / fan_in`, embeddings get `lr * embedding_lr_multiplier`, and element-wise parameters get `lr`; parameter groups (including `group_overrides`) are split by multiplier when the optimizer is built. Use it with `InitMethod.nanochat`. `named_param_shapes` in `olmo_core.nn.transformer.mup` classifies parameters, and `src/examples/mup/coord_check.py` runs a width coordinate check.
+- Added a base-model mode to `MuPConfig`: `MuPConfig.from_base_model(model)` stores each weight-matrix role's fan-in in a base model as `base_fan_ins`, and each matrix then gets `lr * base_fan_in / fan_in`, so every learning rate is exactly `lr` in the base model. Roles (`named_matrix_roles` in `olmo_core.nn.transformer.mup`) match matrices across models of different width and depth by block kind and path within the block.
+- Added the CompletedP (Complete^(d)P) parameterization from "Completed Hyperparameter Transfer across Modules, Width, Depth, Batch & Duration" (arXiv:2512.22382). Set `TransformerConfig.completedp` (`CompletedPConfig`: `base_width`, `base_depth`, `alpha`) on the model to scale every residual branch by `(n_layers / base_depth) ** -alpha` and the `normal` init of hidden matrices, the LM head and in-block matrices with a fixed output size (MoE routers, KDA `f_proj_1` / `g_proj_1`) by width. Then set `completedp` (`CompletedPOptimConfig`) on `AdamWConfig`, `SkipStepAdamWConfig` or `OLMoDDPOptimizerConfig` to give each parameter group its own learning rate, AdamW epsilon and weight decay by role, width and depth, plus batch-size and training-duration scaling of those and of the betas. Supported for dense default / reordered-norm / peri-norm blocks and OLMoDDP MoE-v2 blocks. `OLMoDDPTransformerBlock` now accepts `attention_residual_alpha` and `feed_forward_residual_alpha`, and folds them into the branch output norm's gains when it can (`LayerNorm.output_scale`, supported by `LayerNorm` and `RMSNorm`). `src/examples/completedp/` has a width/depth coordinate check and a hero-architecture check.
+- Added `CompletedPConfig.from_base_model()`, which records the fan-in of every weight matrix of the base model (`CompletedPConfig.base_block_fan_ins`). Each matrix's width ratio is then its fan-in over the same matrix's fan-in in the base model, instead of over `base_width`, so the base model gets exactly the base init and hyperparameters, including matrices whose fan-in isn't `d_model` (e.g. an MLP's down projection). Configs without `base_block_fan_ins` keep the previous rule and log a warning.
+- Added `CompletedPConfig.fixed_kv_width` (default off). When set, softmax attention's `w_k` and `w_v` are readout matrices, with the output-weight init and epsilon, for models whose key/value width (`n_kv_heads * head_dim`) is the same at every size.
 
 ### Fixed
 
+- The extra token rows of `SplitVocabEmbedding` (`TransformerConfig.n_extra_vocab > 0`) are now initialized by the model's init method like the base rows, instead of always with `init_std`, so they start at the same scale under `nanochat`, `llama`, `llama_depth`, `fan_in` and `normalized` init. The `normal` init is unchanged. muP and CompletedP now classify both rows as embeddings instead of raising.
 - Fixed int32 pointer-offset overflow in the valid-prefix SwiGLU Triton kernels (forward, dynamic-row forward, and backward). Row and column indices are widened to int64 before stride multiplication, so no-gradient MoE activation buffers with 2^31 or more elements (for example 1,048,576 rows by 2,048 BF16 columns) no longer read or write wrapped addresses.
 - Activation checkpointing now preserves the RNG state across recomputation whenever dropout is active (including `ResidualStream.masked_dropout`), so the recomputed forward replays the same dropout masks as the original forward instead of drawing new ones. Previously this was done only for EMO routing.
 - Preserve OLMoDDP inference rounding in newly exported HF models, including packed dense/shared projections, packed SwiGLU, and architecture-specific BF16 TransformerEngine index-map combination; serialize the mode and retain legacy HF configs' existing numerics. CUDA inference without Triton uses the Torch activation fallback.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## Unreleased

### Added

- Added `UnshardedModelExportCallback` and `load_unsharded_model_state()`, which write an unsharded `model.safetensors` (plus the config) into every permanent checkpoint so evaluation can read one file instead of the sharded state.



## [v3.0.0](https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/releases/tag/v3.0.0) - 2026-09-30

### Added

===NEW===
- Fixed int32 pointer-offset overflow in the valid-prefix SwiGLU Triton kernels (forward, dynamic-row forward, and backward). Row and column indices are widened to int64 before stride multiplication, so no-gradient MoE activation buffers with 2^31 or more elements (for example 1,048,576 rows by 2,048 BF16 columns) no longer read or write wrapped addresses.
- Activation checkpointing now preserves the RNG state across recomputation whenever dropout is active (including `ResidualStream.masked_dropout`), so the recomputed forward replays the same dropout masks as the original forward instead of drawing new ones. Previously this was done only for EMO routing.
- Preserve OLMoDDP inference rounding in newly exported HF models, including packed dense/shared projections, packed SwiGLU, and architecture-specific BF16 TransformerEngine index-map combination; serialize the mode and retain legacy HF configs' existing numerics. CUDA inference without Triton uses the Torch activation fallback.
- Allow experiment workloads to configure the distributed timeout for long rank-zero dataset preparation while preserving the 15-minute default.
- Preserve 16-byte parameter alignment in OLMoDDP flat model buffers so compiled kernels remain valid after small BF16 parameters are packed.
- Keep no-EP and rowwise-NVSHMEM shared-expert CUDA stream switching outside compiled graphs to avoid Torch 2.13 backward failures after a separately compiled loss, while retaining compiled expert math and stream overlap.
- Metadata-backed packed datasets now include sidecar content hashes in packing-cache keys and dataset fingerprints, invalidating stale boundaries even after same-size corrections. Document lengths preserve EOS/BOS padding segmentation. Local array-backed defaults are unchanged (https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/pull/843).



## [v3.0.0](https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/releases/tag/v3.0.0) - 2026-09-30

### Added

- Added `use_array_if_local` to `pack_documents_into_instances`, `segment_documents_into_instances`, `NumpyPackedFSLDataset` and `NumpyPackedFSLDatasetConfig`, forwarded to `iter_document_indices`. Set it to `False` to take document boundaries from the source metadata file instead of inferring them by scanning the token array for the EOS token. Inferring is only correct when every document is EOS-terminated: a producer that truncates documents and drops the terminator with the tail causes the affected document to merge with the one after it, and `LongDocStrategy.truncate` then keeps only the head of the merged span, so the following document never reaches training. Measured on an SFT cache, 97.98% of tokens reached instances via the inferred path versus 100.00% via the metadata file, with an identical maximum document length. Whenever the metadata boundaries are the effective source -- set explicitly, or because the source is a URL, for which `iter_document_indices` always reads the metadata -- `doc_lens` is derived from them rather than by rescanning the packed tokens for EOS, so the block-diagonal attention mask cannot merge an unterminated document into the one after it. The hazard is now documented on `iter_document_indices`. Default behavior is unchanged.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## Unreleased

### Added

- Added `UnshardedModelExportCallback` and `load_unsharded_model_state()`, which write an unsharded `model.safetensors` (plus the config) into every permanent checkpoint so evaluation can read one file instead of the sharded state.



## [v3.0.0](https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/releases/tag/v3.0.0) - 2026-09-30

### Added

===NEW===
- Fixed int32 pointer-offset overflow in the valid-prefix SwiGLU Triton kernels (forward, dynamic-row forward, and backward). Row and column indices are widened to int64 before stride multiplication, so no-gradient MoE activation buffers with 2^31 or more elements (for example 1,048,576 rows by 2,048 BF16 columns) no longer read or write wrapped addresses.
- Activation checkpointing now preserves the RNG state across recomputation whenever dropout is active (including `ResidualStream.masked_dropout`), so the recomputed forward replays the same dropout masks as the original forward instead of drawing new ones. Previously this was done only for EMO routing.
- Preserve OLMoDDP inference rounding in newly exported HF models, including packed dense/shared projections, packed SwiGLU, and architecture-specific BF16 TransformerEngine index-map combination; serialize the mode and retain legacy HF configs' existing numerics. CUDA inference without Triton uses the Torch activation fallback.
- Allow experiment workloads to configure the distributed timeout for long rank-zero dataset preparation while preserving the 15-minute default.
- Preserve 16-byte parameter alignment in OLMoDDP flat model buffers so compiled kernels remain valid after small BF16 parameters are packed.
- Keep no-EP and rowwise-NVSHMEM shared-expert CUDA stream switching outside compiled graphs to avoid Torch 2.13 backward failures after a separately compiled loss, while retaining compiled expert math and stream overlap.
- Metadata-backed packed datasets now include sidecar content hashes in packing-cache keys and dataset fingerprints, invalidating stale boundaries even after same-size corrections. Document lengths preserve EOS/BOS padding segmentation. Local array-backed defaults are unchanged (https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/pull/843).



## [v3.0.0](https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/releases/tag/v3.0.0) - 2026-09-30

### Added

- Added `use_array_if_local` to `pack_documents_into_instances`, `segment_documents_into_instances`, `NumpyPackedFSLDataset` and `NumpyPackedFSLDatasetConfig`, forwarded to `iter_document_indices`. Set it to `False` to take document boundaries from the source metadata file instead of inferring them by scanning the token array for the EOS token. Inferring is only correct when every document is EOS-terminated: a producer that truncates documents and drops the terminator with the tail causes the affected document to merge with the one after it, and `LongDocStrategy.truncate` then keeps only the head of the merged span, so the following document never reaches training. Measured on an SFT cache, 97.98% of tokens reached instances via the inferred path versus 100.00% via the metadata file, with an identical maximum document length. Whenever the metadata boundaries are the effective source -- set explicitly, or because the source is a URL, for which `iter_document_indices` always reads the metadata -- `doc_lens` is derived from them rather than by rescanning the packed tokens for EOS, so the block-diagonal attention mask cannot merge an unterminated document into the one after it. The hazard is now documented on `iter_document_indices`. Default behavior is unchanged.

"""
Per-parameter shapes used by the muP learning-rate rules.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Dict, Optional, Tuple

import torch.nn as nn

from olmo_core.config import StrEnum
from olmo_core.exceptions import OLMoConfigurationError

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .model import Transformer

__all__ = [
    "ParamKind",
    "ParamShape",
    "named_param_shapes",
    "named_matrix_roles",
    "matrix_fan_ins_by_role",
]

# Name segments added by wrappers (activation checkpointing, ``torch.compile``) that don't change
# what a parameter is.
_WRAPPER_SEGMENTS = ("_checkpoint_wrapped_module", "_orig_mod")


class ParamKind(StrEnum):
    """
    How muP treats a parameter.
    """

    matrix = "matrix"
    """
    A weight matrix whose fan-in grows with width, such as a linear layer, an expert weight, or a
    router.
    """

    embedding = "embedding"
    """
    An embedding table. Its one-hot input has a fixed size, so it does not scale with width.
    """

    vector = "vector"
    """
    An element-wise parameter: norm gains, biases, per-head or per-channel scalars, and depthwise
    convolution taps.
    """


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ParamShape:
    """
    The muP role of a parameter and, for matrices, its logical fan-in and fan-out.
    """

    kind: ParamKind
    fan_in: Optional[int] = None
    fan_out: Optional[int] = None

units.title: 单元十：高级主题与二次开发

input.head: 704625ad94a7c8bc93f9bea7a0b865b9a0c3d44e
input.rationale: 本轮增量（075a7892d..704625ad9，仅提交 #955 "Implement NanoChat Init, muP, complete(d)P"）引入三套现代参数化方案：InitMethod.nanochat 谱条件初始化（init.py 大幅扩展，attention/__init__.py、kda.py、recurrent.py、model.py 的 SplitVocabEmbedding 附加行初始化同步修改）、muP 学习率（新增 nn/transformer/mup.py 与 optim/mup.py，OptimConfig 新增 mup 字段并在 build 时按 lr 乘数切分参数组）、CompletedP 参数化（新增 nn/transformer/completedp.py 与 optim/completedp.py，TransformerConfig 新增 completedp 字段，LayerNorm 新增 output_scale），并附带 src/examples/mup、src/examples/completedp 坐标检查示例与大量新测试。据此决策：已生成的九篇讲义中，u1-l2、u2-l1、u2-l3 引用的文件完全未变，标记 keep；u1-l1 引用的 CHANGELOG 在其 L41 锚点上方插入 7 行新增条目（L41→约 L48），u1-l3 的 TransformerConfig 锚点因新增 import 下移一位且源码树新增 examples/mup、examples/completedp 目录与四个新库模块，u1-l4 与 u3-l2 引用的 transformer/config.py 大量行号偏移且 u3-l2 所讲的 TransformerConfig 类本身新增 completedp 字段，u2-l2 引用的 optim/config.py、adamw.py、recurrent.py 行号均有偏移，u3-l1 引用的 model.py 构造与初始化代码改动，这六篇标记 update 以刷新锚点并补充新内容；u3-l6 与 u5-l1 尚未生成，扩展其主题以覆盖 nanochat 与 mup/completedp 字段后保持 new；u3-l4 主题补充 LayerNorm.output_scale。另按"新增重要机制需要新增讲义"的规则，在高级主题单元新增 u10-l7（nanochat + muP，依赖 u3-l6/u5-l1）与 u10-l8（CompletedP，依赖 u10-l7/u3-l2）两篇，与 float8 等横切高级主题并列；其余未生成讲义的计划与引用文件均不受本次改动影响，保持 new。

learning_goals: 说出 OLMo-core 在 OLMo 生态（训练库、Docker 镜像、官方脚本、HF 集成）中的位置

lectures.title: OLMo-core 是什么：项目定位与全景图
lectures.topic: 介绍 OLMo-core 的定位：AI2 的 OLMo 系列模型训练库，覆盖 Transformer 组件、分布式训练、数据加载与评测；梳理它与 OLMo 模型发布、Docker 镜像、官方训练脚本之间的关系。

learning_goals: 从源码 pip install -e '.[all]' 完成开发安装
用 pytest -v src/ 跑测试并理解 GPU 测试自动跳过机制
使用 make style / make checks 保持代码风格
lectures.practice_task: 完成开发安装，运行 pytest -v src/test/olmo_core/config_test.py（或任一非 GPU 测试文件）确认环境可用，再运行 make style-check 观察格式检查输出。
lectures.title: 环境搭建：安装、测试与代码检查
lectures.topic: 讲解如何安装 OLMo-core（含可选依赖）、如何用 pytest 运行测试（GPU 测试无 GPU 时自动跳过）、以及 make style/lint/type-check 等代码检查工具链。

learning_goals: 画出 src/olmo_core 下各子包的职责一览图
说明 src/test 如何镜像源码结构
在源码树中快速定位'模型、数据、训练、分布式'四类代码的位置
lectures.practice_task: 对照本讲的结构图，在本地仓库中找到 TransformerConfig、TrainerConfig、NumpyDatasetConfig 三个类的定义文件，并记录它们的文件路径和行号。
lectures.title: 源码地图：目录结构与测试布局
lectures.topic: 带读者走一遍 src/olmo_core 的目录结构：config.py、nn/（模型）、data/（数据）、train/（训练）、distributed/（并行与 checkpoint）、optim/（优化器）、eval/、generate/、launch/、kernels/，以及 src/test 与源码一一镜像的组织方式。

learning_goals: 读懂 ExperimentConfig 如何把 model/dataset/data_loader/train_module/trainer 组合成一次实验
理解 build() 模式：从 Config 构建真实组件
了解 torchrun 启动与 prepare_training_environment/teardown_training_environment 的作用
lectures.practice_task: 通读 src/examples/llm/train.py，画出从 ExperimentConfig 到 trainer.fit() 的调用流程图；然后尝试用 torchrun --nproc-per-node=1 以最小配置 dry-run 该脚本（或解释它需要哪些数据与环境前提）。
lectures.title: 跑通第一个训练例子：examples/llm/train.py
lectures.topic: 精读自包含示例 src/examples/llm/train.py，理解一个完整训练实验如何由 model、dataset、data_loader、train_module、trainer 五个 Config 组装而成，并用 torchrun 启动。

learning_goals: 掌握 Config 的 as_dict/save/load/merge 等核心方法
理解为什么所有配置都是可序列化的嵌套 dataclass
能自定义一个继承 Config 的实验配置类
lectures.practice_task: 定义一个继承 Config 的 MyExperimentConfig（含一个嵌套的 TransformerConfig 字段），将它保存为 YAML 再加载回来，验证往返一致；再用 merge() 用 dotlist 覆盖某个嵌套字段。
lectures.title: Config 基类：一切配置的基石
lectures.topic: 讲解 src/olmo_core/config.py 中的 Config dataclass 基类：YAML/JSON 序列化、嵌套组合、以及为什么整个库都用 @dataclass 配置类。

learning_goals: 理解 Registrable 注册机制与 type 字段反序列化
解释优化器、调度器、attention backend、data loader 为何都设计成多态 Config 字段
能为自定义子类注册名称并通过 YAML 选择它
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 AdamWConfig 的注册代码，然后自定义一个注册到同一基类的优化器配置（例如带权重衰减开关的 MyAdamWConfig），验证用 save/load 往返后 build() 得到的是你的子类实例。
lectures.title: Registrable 与多态配置字段
lectures.topic: 讲解来自 dataclass-extensions 的 Registrable 混入：基类 Config 如何通过 type 字段在运行时解析到不同子类，这是优化器、调度器、注意力后端、数据加载器可插拔的基础。

learning_goals: 掌握 --train_module.optim.lr=6e-3 形式的命令行覆盖原理
读懂 script_utils.py 中官方脚本的通用 CLI 与训练流程
能写出接受 dotlist 覆盖的自定义入口脚本
lectures.practice_task: 基于 script_utils.get_cli_parser 写一个最小入口脚本：从 YAML 加载 ExperimentConfig，接受命令行 dotlist 覆盖，打印最终配置并保存为 YAML。
lectures.title: 命令行覆盖与 dotlist 合并：官方脚本入口的秘密
lectures.topic: 讲解 --train_module.optim.lr=6e-3 这类命令行覆盖如何通过 Config.merge() 的 dotlist 机制实现，以及 src/olmo_core/script_utils.py 提供的 ExperimentConfig 与 main() 入口模式。

units.title: 单元二：配置系统——贯穿全库的设计模式

learning_goals: 跟踪一次 forward 中数据的流动路径
理解 Transformer 与 TransformerBlock 的职责划分
对比 OLMo-core 实现与经典 Transformer 的差异点
lectures.practice_task: 从 model.py 的 forward 出发手绘数据流图（embedding → N 个 block → norm → lm_head → loss），标注每个张量的形状变化；再写一小段代码构建 olmo2_14M 配置的模型并打印每层输出形状。
lectures.title: Transformer 总体架构：从 token 到 logits
lectures.topic: 精读 nn/transformer/model.py 的 Transformer 类与 block.py 的 TransformerBlock，理解残差流、block 堆叠和前向传播主链路。

learning_goals: 读懂 TransformerConfig 中每个字段对应的模型结构含义
使用 olmo2_190M/olmo3_7B 等工厂方法快速构建模型配置
理解 Config 工厂方法 + kwargs 覆盖的复用模式
lectures.practice_task: 对比 olmo2_1B 与 olmo3_1B 工厂方法的差异（层数、头数、注意力类型等），并用 kwargs 把 olmo2_14M 改造成自定义小模型，build 后统计参数量。
lectures.title: TransformerConfig 与预置架构工厂方法
lectures.topic: 讲解 TransformerConfig 的字段含义（含本轮新增的可选 completedp 参数化字段，详见 u10-l8）与 olmo2_1M 到 olmo2_32B、olmo3 系列等预置工厂方法，以及 build() 如何初始化一个模型。

learning_goals: 理解 Attention 基类与 MultiHeadAttention 的接口约定
说明各 attention backend 的适用场景与依赖
通过 Config 切换 attention 实现并验证输出一致
lectures.practice_task: 分别用默认 backend 与 flash attention backend 构建同一 TransformerConfig 的模型，对比前向输出是否一致（容差内），并记录两者的内存与速度差异（无 GPU 可用 CPU 可跑的 backend 对比）。
lectures.title: 注意力机制与可插拔后端
lectures.topic: 讲解 nn/attention/ 的抽象：base.py 的注意力基类、backend.py 的后端枚举、flash attention/ring attention 等实现，以及后端如何通过 Registrable 配置切换。

learning_goals: 理解 SwiGLU 前馈、LayerNorm/RMSNorm、RoPE 的实现细节
弄清权重共享与非共享 lm_head 的配置方式
能替换或自定义其中任一组件
lectures.practice_task: 实现一个自定义 FeedForward 变体（如把 SwiGLU 换成 GeGLU），注册进 Registrable 体系，并验证它能被 TransformerConfig 选中且前向形状正确。
lectures.title: 核心组件：前馈网络、LayerNorm、RoPE 与 LM Head
lectures.topic: 逐一讲解 feed_forward.py（SwiGLU 等）、layer_norm.py（含本轮新增的 LayerNorm.output_scale 增益缩放）、rope.py（旋转位置编码）、lm_head.py 与 embedding.py 这些标准组件的实现与配置项。

learning_goals: 说明 MoE层的路由、专家计算与负载均衡损失如何协作
对比 dropless MoE 与普通 MLP 的取舍
用 MoE TransformerConfig 构建一个小模型
lectures.practice_task: 把一个 dense 的 olmo2 小模型配置改造成 MoE 版本（如 8 专家 top-2），build 后打印专家路由分布，并解释负载均衡 loss 的数值含义。
lectures.title: 混合专家（MoE）：路由、专家与负载均衡
lectures.topic: 讲解 nn/moe/ 的 MoE 实现：router 的负载均衡路由、专家 MLP、并行专家（parallel_mlp.py）与 MoE 辅助损失。

learning_goals: 理解 init 功能（标准差缩放等）如何按参数类型应用
复现同一 seed 下的确定性初始化
说明本轮新增 InitMethod.nanochat 的谱条件公式 std = 1/√fan_in · min(1, √(fan_out/fan_in)) 及其覆盖的组件（attention、KDA、GatedDeltaNet、dense/MoE 前馈）
自定义新参数类型的初始化方案
lectures.practice_task: 用相同 init_seed 构建两次模型验证权重完全一致；再修改初始化配置观察参数分布（均值/方差）的变化，并用 seed_all() 解释全局可复现性；最后分别用 normal 与 nanochat 初始化同一小模型，对比各层权重标准差与 fan_in/fan_out 的关系。
lectures.title: 模型初始化：权重从哪里来
lectures.topic: 讲解 nn/transformer/init.py 的参数初始化方案（normal、llama、fan_in、normalized，以及本轮新增的 nanochat 谱条件初始化与 nanochat_std/init_linear_nanochat）与 init_seed 如何保证可复现。

learning_goals: 解释 .npy 预分词数据格式与内存映射的收益
区分 FSL/TSL/padded 等数据集变体
用 NumpyDataLoaderConfig 组装训练与验证数据加载
lectures.practice_task: 用随机 token 构造一个小型 .npy 数据集文件，通过 NumpyDatasetConfig + NumpyDataLoaderConfig 构建加载器，遍历打印几个 batch 的形状。
lectures.title: NumpyDataset：预分词数据的内存映射加载
lectures.topic: 讲解 data/numpy_dataset.py 的内存映射 .npy 数据集家族与 data_loader.py 的 NumpyDataLoader，包括 TokenizerConfig 与 collator 的配合。

learning_goals: 理解 TokenSource → InstanceSource → ComposableDataLoader 三层抽象
掌握切片、采样、按比例混合、按阶段切分的组合用法
能用 visualize() 调试自己的数据源树
lectures.practice_task: 用 composable API 搭建一个包含两个数据源、按 3:1 混合、再切出前 80% 做训练的数据管线，用 InstanceSource.visualize() 打印源树并验证采样比例。
lectures.title: Composable 数据管线：TokenSource → InstanceSource → DataLoader
lectures.topic: 讲解新一代数据 API data/composable/：TokenSource、InstanceSource 的切片/采样/混合/packing 组合子，以及 ComposableDataLoader 的拼装与 visualize 可视化。

learning_goals: 读懂 source mixture 配置如何把多个数据源按权重组合
了解 dolma17 等预置 mix 与 curriculum（分阶段）用法
为自定义语料编写一个 mixture 配置
lectures.practice_task: 阅读一个预置 .txt mixture 文件的格式，然后为你自己的两个 .npy 数据源编写等价的 mixture 配置，并用它构建 ComposableDataLoader 验证各源的实际占比。
lectures.title: 数据混合：source_mixture 与预置 mixes
lectures.topic: 讲解 source_mixture.py 的数据混合机制、data/mixes/ 中 OLMo 官方训练配方的组织方式，以及如何用混合比例与课程学习式切分组织多源数据。

learning_goals: 掌握 OptimConfig 家族的公共字段与参数组覆盖机制
理解 build() 如何从配置生成真实优化器实例
为不同参数组设置不同超参
了解本轮新增的 OptimConfig.mup / OptimConfig.completedp 可选字段的作用入口
lectures.practice_task: 创建 AdamWConfig 并用 OptimGroupOverride 给 embedding 与 lm_head 设置不同的权重衰减，build 后打印优化器的参数组划分验证生效。
lectures.title: 优化器配置体系：AdamW、Lion 与参数组覆盖
lectures.topic: 讲解 optim/ 包：OptimConfig 基类（含本轮新增的 mup/completedp 可选字段，深入实现见 u10-l7/u10-l8）、AdamWConfig/LionConfig/MuonConfig 等实现，以及 OptimGroupOverride 如何对特定参数组覆盖超参。

learning_goals: 理解 warmup + cosine decay 等调度曲线的参数化方式
说明调度器与 step/总步数的联动关系
绘制并验证自定义调度曲线
lectures.practice_task: 构建 CosWithWarmup 调度器，绘制 0 到总步数的完整学习率曲线，并与官方训练脚本中的调度参数对照，解释 anneal 阶段为何要重设 lr。
lectures.title: 学习率调度器
lectures.topic: 讲解 optim/scheduler.py 的 CosWithWarmup 等学习率调度器：如何按 step 计算即时学习率、warmup 与衰减的配置方式。

learning_goals: 理解 loss spike 检测触发的跳步逻辑
掌握梯度裁剪在优化器层的实现位置
用 grad_debug 工具检查异常梯度
lectures.practice_task: 用一个小模型构造一次人为的 loss spike（注入异常梯度），观察 SkipStepOptimizer 是否触发跳步，并打印其内部计数状态。
lectures.title: SkipStepOptimizer：loss spike 检测与梯度裁剪
lectures.topic: 讲解 SkipStepOptimizer 包装器：梯度裁剪、loss spike 检测与跳步策略，以及 grad_debug.py 的梯度诊断工具。

learning_goals: 跟踪 Trainer.fit() 中一个 step 的完整执行顺序
理解 Duration、LoadStrategy 等核心枚举的语义
说明指标收集与跨 rank 归约（ReduceType）机制
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 Trainer.fit() 源码，列出一个训练 step 内所有关键阶段（数据获取、前向、反向、优化器 step、指标、checkpoint）的先后顺序，并标出回调钩子插入的位置。
lectures.title: Trainer 训练循环剖析
lectures.topic: 精读 train/trainer.py 的 Trainer 类与 TrainerConfig：训练主循环、step 管理、指标收集与归约、Duration（按 step/token/epoch 停训）语义。

learning_goals: 理解 TrainModule 抽象与 TransformerTrainModule 的分工
说明并行配置为何挂在 train module 上
梳理一次 forward/backward/optimizer step 的代码路径
lectures.practice_task: 构建一个最小 TransformerTrainModuleConfig（单卡 DP），配合随机数据手动执行一次 train_step，打印 loss 与优化器状态，验证你理解的调用链与源码一致。
lectures.title: TransformerTrainModule：前向、反向与并行设置的汇聚点
lectures.topic: 讲解 train/train_module/ 的 TrainModule 抽象与 TransformerTrainModule：它包装模型、优化器与并行策略（DP/TP/PP/CP/EP 配置都存放在此），并实现 forward/backward 逻辑。

learning_goals: 掌握 Callback 基类的全部钩子及其触发时机
理解内置回调（checkpointer、evaluator、speed monitor 等）的组合方式
编写自定义回调并挂载到 Trainer
lectures.practice_task: 实现一个自定义 Callback，在每个 step 结束时打印当前 step、loss 与吞吐，挂到 TrainerConfig 上跑一次小训练，验证钩子触发顺序与你的预期一致。
lectures.title: 回调系统：如何扩展训练循环
lectures.topic: 讲解 train/callbacks/ 的 Callback 钩子体系与丰富的内置回调：checkpoint、评估、日志（WandB/Comet/console）、速度与显存监控、序列长度调度等。

learning_goals: 理解分布式 checkpoint 的保存/恢复与重分片
掌握 LoadStrategy 各取值的使用场景
实现一次完整的训练中断与续训
lectures.practice_task: 跑一个小训练到第 N 步保存 checkpoint，模拟中断后用 LoadStrategy.new_cmd 改变配置续训，对比两次运行的 loss 曲线是否无缝衔接。
lectures.title: Checkpoint 体系：保存、恢复与断点续训
lectures.topic: 讲解 train/checkpoint.py 的 Checkpointer 与 distributed/checkpoint/ 的分布式保存/加载（含不同文件系统后端）、异步 checkpoint 与 LoadStrategy 恢复策略。

learning_goals: 区分 DDP、FSDP、HSDP 的分片与梯度同步差异
通过 DataParallelConfig 切换并行策略
理解 gradient reduction 与 fsdp wrap policy 的配置
lectures.practice_task: 分别用 DDP 与 FSDP 配置（单进程模拟或 CPU 多进程）构建训练设置，对比优化器状态中参数分片的差异，并解释 HSDP 与 FSDP 的参数量取舍。
lectures.title: 数据并行：DDP、FSDP 与 HSDP
lectures.topic: 讲解 distributed/parallel/data_parallel.py 的 DataParallelType（DDP/FSDP/HSDP）与对应的 train module 设置，理解分片策略与梯度归约。

learning_goals: 说明张量/流水线/上下文/专家并行各自切分的对象
理解多维并行组合时的进程组划分
为模型配置组合并行策略
理解张量并行下 CrossEntropyLoss 的跨 rank 归约：为何规约结果是 Partial 而非 Replicate，mean 归约为何要除以全局有效 token 数
lectures.practice_task: 阅读官方 OLMo-2 32B 脚本中的并行配置组合，画出 8 卡情况下各并行维度的进程组划分示意图，并解释为何 attention 适合 TP 而 MoE 专家适合 EP；再对照 cross_entropy_loss.py 中 TP 损失归约的修复（Partial 布局 + 全局有效 token 数归一化），说明若把规约结果误标为 Replicate 会发生什么。
lectures.title: 张量、流水线、上下文与专家并行
lectures.topic: 总览其余并行维度：tensor_parallel、pipeline_parallel（含 pipeline train module）、context_parallel（ring attention）、expert_parallel，以及它们如何与 DP 组合成多维并行；并结合 cross_entropy_loss.py 讲清张量并行下损失如何跨 rank 归约（Partial 输出布局与按全局有效 token 数归一化，对应 075a7892d 的修复）。

learning_goals: 理解进程组创建与 world/rank 的管理方式
使用 olmo_core.testing.distributed 编写多进程测试
排查常见的分布式初始化问题
lectures.practice_task: 基于 olmo_core.testing/distributed.py 的工具写一个双进程的小测试：各自持有一半数据，all-gather 后验证合并结果，并用 pytest 跑通它。
lectures.title: 分布式工具与测试基础设施
lectures.topic: 讲解 distributed/utils.py 的进程组管理（init_distributed、get_rank 等）、distributed/nn.py 的分布式原语，以及 testing/distributed.py 提供的多进程测试工具。

learning_goals: 掌握 Evaluator 抽象接口与 LMEvaluator 的评估循环
理解 task groups 如何组织下游评测
用 DownstreamEvaluatorCallback 在训练中周期性评测
lectures.practice_task: 构建一个迷你 LMEvaluator（用小模型 + 少量随机 prompt 计算 loss 与 ppl），通过 evaluator callback 挂到训练循环，观察每轮评估指标的变化。
lectures.title: 评测框架：Evaluator 与 LMEvaluator
lectures.topic: 讲解 eval/ 包的 Evaluator 抽象、LMEvaluator 的困惑度评估、task_groups 与训练中的 DownstreamEvaluatorCallback/LMEvaluatorCallback。

learning_goals: 理解 generation module 的采样与 KV cache 机制
用 olmo_core.generate.chat 交互式加载 checkpoint 推理
对比 OLMo-core 生成与 HF/vLLM 推理的适用场景
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 generate/generation_module/transformer/generation_module.py 的循环逻辑，用随机初始化的小模型（或公开 checkpoint）跑一次自回归生成，并调整 sampling 参数观察输出变化。
lectures.title: 生成与 Chat：在 OLMo-core 里做自回归推理
lectures.topic: 讲解 generate/ 包：generation_module 的自回归生成循环、sampling.py 的采样策略（temperature/top-p）以及 chat.py 的交互式聊天入口。

learning_goals: 读懂 ExperimentConfig + main() 的官方脚本骨架
理解预训练、midtrain、anneal、long-context 各阶段的配置差异
通过命令行 dotlist 复现/修改官方训练配置
lectures.practice_task: 选一个 OLMo-3 7B pretrain 脚本，画出其配置树（模型/数据/优化器/并行/回调），找出 5 个你能通过命令行安全覆盖的字段并实际覆盖跑 dry-run。
lectures.title: 官方训练脚本解析：如何复现 OLMo-2/OLMo-3
lectures.topic: 以 scripts/official/ 下的 OLMo-2 32B 与 OLMo-3 7B/32B 脚本为例，讲解官方脚本如何用 ExperimentConfig 组装完整配方并用 torchrun 启动。

learning_goals: 掌握 launch/train/train_single/prep/dry_run 子命令的工作方式

units.title: 单元十：高级主题与二次开发

call_9676b74495234259bf8a8ed6.head: 704625ad94a7c8bc93f9bea7a0b865b9a0c3d44e
call_9676b74495234259bf8a8ed6.rationale: 本轮增量（075a7892d..704625ad9，仅提交 #955 "Implement NanoChat Init, muP, complete(d)P"）引入三套现代参数化方案：InitMethod.nanochat 谱条件初始化（init.py 大幅扩展，attention/__init__.py、kda.py、recurrent.py、model.py 的 SplitVocabEmbedding 附加行初始化同步修改）、muP 学习率（新增 nn/transformer/mup.py 与 optim/mup.py，OptimConfig 新增 mup 字段并在 build 时按 lr 乘数切分参数组）、CompletedP 参数化（新增 nn/transformer/completedp.py 与 optim/completedp.py，TransformerConfig 新增 completedp 字段，LayerNorm 新增 output_scale），并附带 src/examples/mup、src/examples/completedp 坐标检查示例与大量新测试。据此决策：已生成的九篇讲义中，u1-l2、u2-l1、u2-l3 引用的文件完全未变，标记 keep；u1-l1 引用的 CHANGELOG 在其 L41 锚点上方插入 7 行新增条目（L41→约 L48），u1-l3 的 TransformerConfig 锚点因新增 import 下移一位且源码树新增 examples/mup、examples/completedp 目录与四个新库模块，u1-l4 与 u3-l2 引用的 transformer/config.py 大量行号偏移且 u3-l2 所讲的 TransformerConfig 类本身新增 completedp 字段，u2-l2 引用的 optim/config.py、adamw.py、recurrent.py 行号均有偏移，u3-l1 引用的 model.py 构造与初始化代码改动，这六篇标记 update 以刷新锚点并补充新内容；u3-l6 与 u5-l1 尚未生成，扩展其主题以覆盖 nanochat 与 mup/completedp 字段后保持 new；u3-l4 主题补充 LayerNorm.output_scale。另按"新增重要机制需要新增讲义"的规则，在高级主题单元新增 u10-l7（nanochat + muP，依赖 u3-l6/u5-l1）与 u10-l8（CompletedP，依赖 u10-l7/u3-l2）两篇，与 float8 等横切高级主题并列；其余未生成讲义的计划与引用文件均不受本次改动影响，保持 new。

自定义新参数类型的初始化方案
lectures.practice_task: 用相同 init_seed 构建两次模型验证权重完全一致；再修改初始化配置观察参数分布（均值/方差）的变化，并用 seed_all() 解释全局可复现性；最后分别用 normal 与 nanochat 初始化同一小模型，对比各层权重标准差与 fan_in/fan_out 的关系。
lectures.title: 模型初始化：权重从哪里来
lectures.topic: 讲解 nn/transformer/init.py 的参数初始化方案（normal、llama、fan_in、normalized，以及本轮新增的 nanochat 谱条件初始化与 nanochat_std/init_linear_nanochat）与 init_seed 如何保证可复现。

learning_goals: 解释 .npy 预分词数据格式与内存映射的收益
区分 FSL/TSL/padded 等数据集变体
用 NumpyDataLoaderConfig 组装训练与验证数据加载
lectures.practice_task: 用随机 token 构造一个小型 .npy 数据集文件，通过 NumpyDatasetConfig + NumpyDataLoaderConfig 构建加载器，遍历打印几个 batch 的形状。
lectures.title: NumpyDataset：预分词数据的内存映射加载
lectures.topic: 讲解 data/numpy_dataset.py 的内存映射 .npy 数据集家族与 data_loader.py 的 NumpyDataLoader，包括 TokenizerConfig 与 collator 的配合。

learning_goals: 理解 TokenSource → InstanceSource → ComposableDataLoader 三层抽象
掌握切片、采样、按比例混合、按阶段切分的组合用法
能用 visualize() 调试自己的数据源树
lectures.practice_task: 用 composable API 搭建一个包含两个数据源、按 3:1 混合、再切出前 80% 做训练的数据管线，用 InstanceSource.visualize() 打印源树并验证采样比例。
lectures.title: Composable 数据管线：TokenSource → InstanceSource → DataLoader
lectures.topic: 讲解新一代数据 API data/composable/：TokenSource、InstanceSource 的切片/采样/混合/packing 组合子，以及 ComposableDataLoader 的拼装与 visualize 可视化。

learning_goals: 读懂 source mixture 配置如何把多个数据源按权重组合
了解 dolma17 等预置 mix 与 curriculum（分阶段）用法
为自定义语料编写一个 mixture 配置
lectures.practice_task: 阅读一个预置 .txt mixture 文件的格式，然后为你自己的两个 .npy 数据源编写等价的 mixture 配置，并用它构建 ComposableDataLoader 验证各源的实际占比。
lectures.title: 数据混合：source_mixture 与预置 mixes
lectures.topic: 讲解 source_mixture.py 的数据混合机制、data/mixes/ 中 OLMo 官方训练配方的组织方式，以及如何用混合比例与课程学习式切分组织多源数据。

learning_goals: 掌握 OptimConfig 家族的公共字段与参数组覆盖机制
理解 build() 如何从配置生成真实优化器实例
为不同参数组设置不同超参
了解本轮新增的 OptimConfig.mup / OptimConfig.completedp 可选字段的作用入口
lectures.practice_task: 创建 AdamWConfig 并用 OptimGroupOverride 给 embedding 与 lm_head 设置不同的权重衰减，build 后打印优化器的参数组划分验证生效。
lectures.title: 优化器配置体系：AdamW、Lion 与参数组覆盖
lectures.topic: 讲解 optim/ 包：OptimConfig 基类（含本轮新增的 mup/completedp 可选字段，深入实现见 u10-l7/u10-l8）、AdamWConfig/LionConfig/MuonConfig 等实现，以及 OptimGroupOverride 如何对特定参数组覆盖超参。

learning_goals: 理解 warmup + cosine decay 等调度曲线的参数化方式
说明调度器与 step/总步数的联动关系
绘制并验证自定义调度曲线
lectures.practice_task: 构建 CosWithWarmup 调度器，绘制 0 到总步数的完整学习率曲线，并与官方训练脚本中的调度参数对照，解释 anneal 阶段为何要重设 lr。
lectures.title: 学习率调度器
lectures.topic: 讲解 optim/scheduler.py 的 CosWithWarmup 等学习率调度器：如何按 step 计算即时学习率、warmup 与衰减的配置方式。

learning_goals: 理解 loss spike 检测触发的跳步逻辑
掌握梯度裁剪在优化器层的实现位置
用 grad_debug 工具检查异常梯度
lectures.practice_task: 用一个小模型构造一次人为的 loss spike（注入异常梯度），观察 SkipStepOptimizer 是否触发跳步，并打印其内部计数状态。
lectures.title: SkipStepOptimizer：loss spike 检测与梯度裁剪
lectures.topic: 讲解 SkipStepOptimizer 包装器：梯度裁剪、loss spike 检测与跳步策略，以及 grad_debug.py 的梯度诊断工具。

learning_goals: 跟踪 Trainer.fit() 中一个 step 的完整执行顺序
理解 Duration、LoadStrategy 等核心枚举的语义
说明指标收集与跨 rank 归约（ReduceType）机制
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 Trainer.fit() 源码，列出一个训练 step 内所有关键阶段（数据获取、前向、反向、优化器 step、指标、checkpoint）的先后顺序，并标出回调钩子插入的位置。
lectures.title: Trainer 训练循环剖析
lectures.topic: 精读 train/trainer.py 的 Trainer 类与 TrainerConfig：训练主循环、step 管理、指标收集与归约、Duration（按 step/token/epoch 停训）语义。

learning_goals: 理解 TrainModule 抽象与 TransformerTrainModule 的分工
说明并行配置为何挂在 train module 上
梳理一次 forward/backward/optimizer step 的代码路径
lectures.practice_task: 构建一个最小 TransformerTrainModuleConfig（单卡 DP），配合随机数据手动执行一次 train_step，打印 loss 与优化器状态，验证你理解的调用链与源码一致。
lectures.title: TransformerTrainModule：前向、反向与并行设置的汇聚点
lectures.topic: 讲解 train/train_module/ 的 TrainModule 抽象与 TransformerTrainModule：它包装模型、优化器与并行策略（DP/TP/PP/CP/EP 配置都存放在此），并实现 forward/backward 逻辑。

learning_goals: 掌握 Callback 基类的全部钩子及其触发时机
理解内置回调（checkpointer、evaluator、speed monitor 等）的组合方式
编写自定义回调并挂载到 Trainer
lectures.practice_task: 实现一个自定义 Callback，在每个 step 结束时打印当前 step、loss 与吞吐，挂到 TrainerConfig 上跑一次小训练，验证钩子触发顺序与你的预期一致。
lectures.title: 回调系统：如何扩展训练循环
lectures.topic: 讲解 train/callbacks/ 的 Callback 钩子体系与丰富的内置回调：checkpoint、评估、日志（WandB/Comet/console）、速度与显存监控、序列长度调度等。

learning_goals: 理解分布式 checkpoint 的保存/恢复与重分片
掌握 LoadStrategy 各取值的使用场景
实现一次完整的训练中断与续训
lectures.practice_task: 跑一个小训练到第 N 步保存 checkpoint，模拟中断后用 LoadStrategy.new_cmd 改变配置续训，对比两次运行的 loss 曲线是否无缝衔接。
lectures.title: Checkpoint 体系：保存、恢复与断点续训
lectures.topic: 讲解 train/checkpoint.py 的 Checkpointer 与 distributed/checkpoint/ 的分布式保存/加载（含不同文件系统后端）、异步 checkpoint 与 LoadStrategy 恢复策略。

learning_goals: 区分 DDP、FSDP、HSDP 的分片与梯度同步差异
通过 DataParallelConfig 切换并行策略
理解 gradient reduction 与 fsdp wrap policy 的配置
lectures.practice_task: 分别用 DDP 与 FSDP 配置（单进程模拟或 CPU 多进程）构建训练设置，对比优化器状态中参数分片的差异，并解释 HSDP 与 FSDP 的参数量取舍。
lectures.title: 数据并行：DDP、FSDP 与 HSDP
lectures.topic: 讲解 distributed/parallel/data_parallel.py 的 DataParallelType（DDP/FSDP/HSDP）与对应的 train module 设置，理解分片策略与梯度归约。

learning_goals: 说明张量/流水线/上下文/专家并行各自切分的对象
理解多维并行组合时的进程组划分
为模型配置组合并行策略
理解张量并行下 CrossEntropyLoss 的跨 rank 归约：为何规约结果是 Partial 而非 Replicate，mean 归约为何要除以全局有效 token 数
lectures.practice_task: 阅读官方 OLMo-2 32B 脚本中的并行配置组合，画出 8 卡情况下各并行维度的进程组划分示意图，并解释为何 attention 适合 TP 而 MoE 专家适合 EP；再对照 cross_entropy_loss.py 中 TP 损失归约的修复（Partial 布局 + 全局有效 token 数归一化），说明若把规约结果误标为 Replicate 会发生什么。
lectures.title: 张量、流水线、上下文与专家并行
lectures.topic: 总览其余并行维度：tensor_parallel、pipeline_parallel（含 pipeline train module）、context_parallel（ring attention）、expert_parallel，以及它们如何与 DP 组合成多维并行；并结合 cross_entropy_loss.py 讲清张量并行下损失如何跨 rank 归约（Partial 输出布局与按全局有效 token 数归一化，对应 075a7892d 的修复）。

learning_goals: 理解进程组创建与 world/rank 的管理方式
使用 olmo_core.testing.distributed 编写多进程测试
排查常见的分布式初始化问题
lectures.practice_task: 基于 olmo_core.testing/distributed.py 的工具写一个双进程的小测试：各自持有一半数据，all-gather 后验证合并结果，并用 pytest 跑通它。
lectures.title: 分布式工具与测试基础设施
lectures.topic: 讲解 distributed/utils.py 的进程组管理（init_distributed、get_rank 等）、distributed/nn.py 的分布式原语，以及 testing/distributed.py 提供的多进程测试工具。

learning_goals: 掌握 Evaluator 抽象接口与 LMEvaluator 的评估循环
理解 task groups 如何组织下游评测
用 DownstreamEvaluatorCallback 在训练中周期性评测
lectures.practice_task: 构建一个迷你 LMEvaluator（用小模型 + 少量随机 prompt 计算 loss 与 ppl），通过 evaluator callback 挂到训练循环，观察每轮评估指标的变化。
lectures.title: 评测框架：Evaluator 与 LMEvaluator
lectures.topic: 讲解 eval/ 包的 Evaluator 抽象、LMEvaluator 的困惑度评估、task_groups 与训练中的 DownstreamEvaluatorCallback/LMEvaluatorCallback。

learning_goals: 理解 generation module 的采样与 KV cache 机制
用 olmo_core.generate.chat 交互式加载 checkpoint 推理
对比 OLMo-core 生成与 HF/vLLM 推理的适用场景
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 generate/generation_module/transformer/generation_module.py 的循环逻辑，用随机初始化的小模型（或公开 checkpoint）跑一次自回归生成，并调整 sampling 参数观察输出变化。
lectures.title: 生成与 Chat：在 OLMo-core 里做自回归推理
lectures.topic: 讲解 generate/ 包：generation_module 的自回归生成循环、sampling.py 的采样策略（temperature/top-p）以及 chat.py 的交互式聊天入口。

learning_goals: 读懂 ExperimentConfig + main() 的官方脚本骨架
理解预训练、midtrain、anneal、long-context 各阶段的配置差异
通过命令行 dotlist 复现/修改官方训练配置
lectures.practice_task: 选一个 OLMo-3 7B pretrain 脚本，画出其配置树（模型/数据/优化器/并行/回调），找出 5 个你能通过命令行安全覆盖的字段并实际覆盖跑 dry-run。
lectures.title: 官方训练脚本解析：如何复现 OLMo-2/OLMo-3
lectures.topic: 以 scripts/official/ 下的 OLMo-2 32B 与 OLMo-3 7B/32B 脚本为例，讲解官方脚本如何用 ExperimentConfig 组装完整配方并用 torchrun 启动。

learning_goals: 掌握 launch/train/train_single/prep/dry_run 子命令的工作方式
理解 prepare_cli_environment 与官方脚本模式的差异
从 template.py 出发定制自己的训练脚本
lectures.practice_task: 复制 template.py 为自己的脚本，定义一个最小 ExperimentConfig，依次跑通 dry_run 命令（无需真实集群），观察生成的配置输出与日志。
lectures.title: 内部训练脚本模板：launch/train/dry_run 工作流
lectures.topic: 讲解 scripts/train/ 的内部脚本模式：prepare_cli_environment 与 launch、train、train_single、prep、dry_run 子命令，以及 template.py 作为起点的用法。

learning_goals: 理解 Gantry recipe 的四步启动流程
掌握 OLMoCoreBeakerImage 与 torch/CUDA 版本的对应关系
用 BeakerLaunchConfig 定制多节点任务（replicas、挂载、pre/post setup）
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 beaker.py 中 OLMoCoreBeakerImage 枚举与 launch() 流程，写出一次 2 节点训练所需的 launch 配置（含 Weka 挂载与 torchrun 包装），并解释 dirty 工作树为何会被拒绝。
lectures.title: Beaker 启动与 Docker 镜像
lectures.topic: 讲解 launch/beaker.py 的 BeakerLaunchConfig/Gantry 启动流程（镜像选择、clone 仓库、pip install、torchrun 包装）、Dockerfile 两阶段构建与 make docker-image。

units.title: 单元九：训练脚本与部署

learning_goals: 理解 float8/mxfp8 训练的收益与风险
掌握通过 Config 启用低精度线性的方式
评估低精度对 loss 稳定性的影响
lectures.practice_task: 对比同一小模型在 fp32 与 mxfp8 线性层配置下的前向输出误差与显存占用，记录数值差异并总结何时值得启用 float8。
lectures.title: 低精度训练：float8 与 mxfp8
lectures.topic: 讲解 float8/ao.py 基于 torchao 的 float8 训练支持与 nn/mxfp8_linear.py 的 mxfp8 线性层，以及 mxfp8_config.py 的配置入口。

learning_goals: 理解 MoE 相关 CUDA 内核（permute/drop、grouped GEMM）要解决的问题
掌握 CUDA 扩展的构建与调用模式
判断一个算子何时值得下沉到自定义内核
lectures.practice_task: 追踪 MoE 前向中 token 路由到专家计算的完整数据搬运路径（permute → grouped GEMM → unpermute），用小规模张量验证 kernels/moe.py 中工具函数与朴素 PyTorch 实现的输出一致性。
lectures.title: 自定义 CUDA 内核：kernels 与 _csrc
lectures.topic: 讲解 kernels/ 包与 nn/_csrc 的自定义 CUDA 扩展：grouped GEMM、MoE token 重排等，以及扩展的构建方式。

learning_goals: 理解 ViT 视觉编码器与连接器如何把图像特征注入语言模型
掌握 image processor 与 token 化的配合
说明 Molmo2 式多模态模型的组件构成
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 vision/config.py 与 image_vit.py，梳理'图像张量 → patch → ViT → connector → 语言模型输入'的形状变化链，用随机图像张量跑通一次视觉侧前向并记录各阶段形状。
lectures.title: 视觉编码器与多模态模型组件
lectures.topic: 讲解 nn/vision/ 的 ViT 视觉编码器、connector、Molmo2 图像处理器与 multimodal.py 如何把视觉能力接入 Transformer。

learning_goals: 理解 message sequence → packing → collator 的多模态数据流
掌握 mixture weights 与多源多模态数据加载的组织方式
为自定义多模态数据源接入训练管线
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 scripts/train/Molmo2-Stage1.py，画出 stage-1 训练的数据与模型配置全景图；再模仿 data/multimodal/ 下任一数据集模块，为一个假设的'图像+文本'数据源写出接入骨架代码。
lectures.title: 多模态数据管线：sequence builder、packing 与 collator
lectures.topic: 讲解 data/multimodal/ 的核心：message sequence 构建、多模态 packing、collator 与 mixture data loader，对应近期合入的 Multimodal 系列改动。

learning_goals: 理解 OLMo-core 与 HF/MaxText 权重的命名与结构映射
掌握 conversion 框架（state converter/mapping）的扩展方式
完成一次双向 checkpoint 转换并验证数值一致
lectures.practice_task: 用 convert_checkpoint_to_hf.py 把一个小型 OLMo-core checkpoint 转成 HF 格式，再用 convert_checkpoint_from_hf.py 转回来，对比两次转换后模型参数是否逐项一致。
lectures.title: Checkpoint 转换：OLMo-core ↔ Hugging Face ↔ MaxText
lectures.topic: 讲解 examples/huggingface/ 的双向转换脚本、nn/conversion/ 的状态转换框架与 nn/maxtext/ 的 MaxText checkpoint 转换。

learning_goals: 按项目规范编写参数化测试与 GPU/分布式测试
用 make style/checks 走完贡献前检查
写出一个符合 Sphinx 规范的公共 API 文档字符串
lectures.practice_task: 为你在 u6-l3 写的自定义回调补充一个 pytest 测试（含 parametrize），补全 Sphinx 风格 docstring，并依次通过 make style-check、make lint-check、make type-check。
lectures.title: 测试体系与贡献流程
lectures.topic: 讲解 src/test 的组织约定（test_* 命名、parametrize、@pytest.mark.gpu、分布式测试工具）、olmo_core.testing 工具与贡献时的格式/lint/类型检查要求，并以 src/test/nn/ddp/helpers.py 为例说明如何把重复的分布式测试整合为共享 helper 与参数化套件。

learning_goals: 理解 muP 的核心主张：按参数在宽度增长时的角色缩放学习率，使超参可跨宽度迁移
掌握 MuPConfig 的两种基准方式：base_width 常数与 from_base_model 记录的 base_fan_ins
说明 named_param_shapes/named_matrix_roles 如何把参数分为 matrix/embedding/vector 三类并计算 lr 乘数
理解 InitMethod.nanochat 谱条件初始化与 muP 的搭配使用
minimal_modules: 按 lr 乘数切分参数组
lectures.practice_task: 给 olmo2 小模型开启 InitMethod.nanochat，并在 AdamWConfig 上挂 MuPConfig(base_width=d_model)，build 后打印优化器每个参数组的 lr_multiplier，验证矩阵参数 lr ∝ base_width/fan_in、embedding 用 embedding_lr_multiplier、逐元素参数保持原 lr；再用 MuPConfig.from_base_model 生成基准配置，确认 base 模型中每个参数的 lr 恰为原始 lr，并阅读 src/examples/mup/coord_check.py 说明坐标检查想观察到什么。
lectures.title: muP 学习率与 NanoChat 初始化：跨宽度迁移超参
lectures.topic: 讲解提交 704625ad9 引入的 muP 支持：optim/mup.py 的 MuPConfig（base_width/base_fan_ins/embedding_lr_multiplier 与 from_base_model）、nn/transformer/mup.py 的参数角色分类、OptimConfig.mup 如何在 build 时按 lr 乘数切分参数组，以及配套的 InitMethod.nanochat 初始化。

learning_goals: 理解 CompletedP 在 muP 之上扩展的宽度、深度、批量与训练时长缩放规则
掌握 CompletedPConfig 的字段（base_width/base_depth/alpha/fixed_kv_width）与 from_base_model 基准模式
说明残差分支按深度缩放如何经 LayerNorm.output_scale 折进归一化增益
用 CompletedPOptimConfig 按角色/宽度/深度为每组设置 lr、eps、weight_decay 与 betas
lectures.practice_task: 给 TransformerConfig 设 completedp=CompletedPConfig(base_width=..., base_depth=..., alpha=1.0)，同时把 CompletedPOptimConfig 挂到 AdamWConfig.completedp，build 后对比 base 模型与加宽/加深模型各参数组的 lr、eps、weight_decay 与 betas 缩放；再用 CompletedPConfig.from_base_model 验证 base 模型恰好得到未缩放的初始化与超参，并解释 LayerNorm.output_scale 如何吸收残差分支的深度缩放。
lectures.title: CompletedP 参数化：跨模块、宽度、深度、批量与时长的超参迁移
lectures.topic: 讲解 nn/transformer/completedp.py 的 CompletedPConfig（宽度/深度缩放、from_base_model、fixed_kv_width）、残差分支缩放如何折入 LayerNorm.output_scale，以及 optim/completedp.py 的 CompletedPOptimConfig 如何按参数角色设置每组 AdamW 超参，并用 src/examples/completedp/ 的坐标检查示例验证。

units.title: 单元十：高级主题与二次开发

data.head: 704625ad94a7c8bc93f9bea7a0b865b9a0c3d44e
data.rationale: 本轮增量（075a7892d..704625ad9，仅提交 #955 "Implement NanoChat Init, muP, complete(d)P"）引入三套现代参数化方案：InitMethod.nanochat 谱条件初始化（init.py 大幅扩展，attention/__init__.py、kda.py、recurrent.py、model.py 的 SplitVocabEmbedding 附加行初始化同步修改）、muP 学习率（新增 nn/transformer/mup.py 与 optim/mup.py，OptimConfig 新增 mup 字段并在 build 时按 lr 乘数切分参数组）、CompletedP 参数化（新增 nn/transformer/completedp.py 与 optim/completedp.py，TransformerConfig 新增 completedp 字段，LayerNorm 新增 output_scale），并附带 src/examples/mup、src/examples/completedp 坐标检查示例与大量新测试。据此决策：已生成的九篇讲义中，u1-l2、u2-l1、u2-l3 引用的文件完全未变，标记 keep；u1-l1 引用的 CHANGELOG 在其 L41 锚点上方插入 7 行新增条目（L41→约 L48），u1-l3 的 TransformerConfig 锚点因新增 import 下移一位且源码树新增 examples/mup、examples/completedp 目录与四个新库模块，u1-l4 与 u3-l2 引用的 transformer/config.py 大量行号偏移且 u3-l2 所讲的 TransformerConfig 类本身新增 completedp 字段，u2-l2 引用的 optim/config.py、adamw.py、recurrent.py 行号均有偏移，u3-l1 引用的 model.py 构造与初始化代码改动，这六篇标记 update 以刷新锚点并补充新内容；u3-l6 与 u5-l1 尚未生成，扩展其主题以覆盖 nanochat 与 mup/completedp 字段后保持 new；u3-l4 主题补充 LayerNorm.output_scale。另按"新增重要机制需要新增讲义"的规则，在高级主题单元新增 u10-l7（nanochat + muP，依赖 u3-l6/u5-l1）与 u10-l8（CompletedP，依赖 u10-l7/u3-l2）两篇，与 float8 等横切高级主题并列；其余未生成讲义的计划与引用文件均不受本次改动影响，保持 new。
